title: Antigen-selective erasure of pathogenic cutaneous immune memory

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a finite treatment that selectively removes or durably disarms the immune cells that remember and restart a particular skin disease. Antigen selectivity means distinguishing cells by the disease-related target they recognize, while preserving useful immune memory. The central target is pathogenic cutaneous T-cell memory; in autoimmune blistering disease, the capability would also need to control the relevant autoreactive B-cell and antibody-producing populations, including populations outside the skin.

Successful erasure could involve deleting pathogenic cells or reprogramming them so that they no longer cause disease. Clinical clearing alone would not establish this capability: disease-associated resident-memory cells can persist in effectively treated psoriasis, and resident memory is implicated in vitiligo recurrence. Some cytokine-directed treatments also reduce resident-memory populations, so the distinction is durable, selective control of disease-maintaining memory rather than an assumption that existing treatments leave every memory population unchanged.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability could allow successfully treated patients to remain well after treatment stops, reducing or eliminating their need for continuing biologics, JAK inhibitors or broad immunosuppression. Its revolutionary feature would be a durable change in the mechanism maintaining disease. The strongest mechanistic grounding in the supplied evidence concerns psoriasis and vitiligo; it does not establish that selective memory editing alone would cure every inflammatory or autoimmune skin disease.

Treatment-free remission would be a major clinical advance, but a two-year demonstration would establish remission over that interval, not lifelong protection against relapse. Removing local immune clones may leave circulating reservoirs, renewed generation of pathogenic specificities or persistent structural-cell programs. In atopic dermatitis, barrier restoration and correction of other disease drivers may therefore be additional requirements rather than automatic consequences of immune-memory editing.

Preserving protective immunity is part of the advance itself. Memory CD8 T cells and natural killer cells contribute to antiviral and antitumor functions, and broadly targeting their maintenance pathways could compromise those functions. A successful vaccine response or recovery from one skin infection would provide useful evidence of retained protection, but neither would establish intact antiviral protection across pathogens or intact cancer surveillance.

Conditional synthesis: psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, vitiligo, alopecia areata, pemphigus and fixed drug eruption are potential application areas named in the research. Their inclusion is a research agenda, not evidence that they share one sufficient target or would respond to one intervention. Success in a T-cell-mediated disease and an autoantibody-mediated disease would demonstrate useful breadth across mechanisms without establishing a universal cure for relapsing dermatoses.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is sufficiently selective, durable control of the pathogenic immune population while sparing protective cells that share its location or survival pathways. The vitiligo evidence illustrates the difficulty: prolonged systemic anti-CD122 treatment can deplete autoreactive resident-memory cells in mice, but also affects other memory T-cell populations. Disrupting a memory-maintenance pathway is therefore not equivalent to recognizing and eliminating only disease-causing specificity.

Engineering synthesis: an antigen-selective intervention needs reliable identification of the relevant disease-driving recognition targets, a way to distinguish pathogenic cells from useful cells, and access to the compartments that sustain recurrence. For psoriasis, the supplied evidence does not establish how completely the relevant antigens and pathogenic populations have been mapped. Antigen identification should remain a disease-specific development requirement rather than a categorical assertion that no psoriasis antigen is known.

Durability requires addressing persistence and replenishment. Local biopsies may miss pathogenic cells elsewhere, and removing one clone may allow another population with the same disease-driving specificity to emerge. Functional reprogramming must remain stable after treatment withdrawal. Persistent tissue programs may also reactivate inflammation even after an immune population has been reduced, making restoration of a healthy tissue state a separate scientific challenge.

Engineering synthesis for the autoantibody arm: selective removal of autoreactive B cells must be connected to durable control of pathogenic antibody production. Relevant B-cell and antibody-producing compartments would need assessment beyond skin-resident cells. The supplied clinical material does not establish which populations a successful pemphigus intervention must reach or whether antigen-specific chimeric autoantibody-receptor T cells have already achieved clinical efficacy.

current_state.text: Su and Liu's July 28, 2025 review describes a vitiligo mouse model in which prolonged systemic anti-CD122 administration over eight weeks depleted autoreactive resident-memory T cells and other memory T-cell populations. This is preclinical evidence that pathogenic memory can be disrupted, with a selectivity limitation. The review warns that systemic IL-15 blockade may impair functions supported by natural killer cells and protective memory CD8 T cells; this concern should not be recast as demonstrated clinical loss of all protective memory.

The same review stated that peer-reviewed clinical outcomes for the phase 2a AMG 714 vitiligo trial were still pending as of 2025. That is a dated account of publication status. The supplied material does not establish whether results subsequently became available by November 1, 2026.

The research attributes one-year withdrawal outcomes to the TRuE-V vitiligo study cited as Harris and colleagues, British Journal of Dermatology, April 17, 2026: among 56 evaluable patients who stopped ruxolitinib cream, 22 reportedly maintained F-VASI75 and 12 maintained F-VASI90. The supplied review had no retained source text for this citation, so these counts, their denominators and the precise endpoint interpretation remain unverified here. Even if confirmed, maintained clinical response after withdrawal would not by itself demonstrate antigen-selective memory erasure.

Ranzinger and Eyerich's May 6, 2025 review describes disease modification in psoriasis as controversial. It documents persistent resident-memory cells after effective treatment while also discussing reductions in these populations with anti-IL-23 treatment. In its discussion of anti-IL-23 withdrawal, it reports that up to 10% of patients maintained treatment response for more than a year. This is a context-specific finding, not a universal ceiling across drugs or selected patient groups, and it does not establish selective eradication of pathogenic memory.

Chen and colleagues' 2025 retrospective-cohort abstract reports a median relapse time of 3.29 months among 400 patients who discontinued an IL-17 inhibitor after achieving PASI 90. Selected early-disease groups had higher one-year drug-free remission. The supplied review could assess the abstract rather than the full paper. These observations support investigation of disease modification in subsets, but the retrospective design and selected subgroup findings do not establish causal immune-memory erasure or a general cure.

For pemphigus, the research attributes to Payne and colleagues' August 2025 report a series of 23 patients receiving DSG3 chimeric autoantibody-receptor T cells, with no consistent improvement in clinical disease activity or anti-DSG3 antibody titers. No source text for that citation was retained for the supplied review. The patient count and outcome therefore remain unverified; they cannot support a categorical conclusion that antigen-specific CAAR-T has failed clinically.

The research also reports that ClinicalTrials.gov listed a July 30, 2026 Blood paper by Nunez and colleagues on CD19 CAR-T without lymphodepletion. The retained page contained only generic site text, so the supplied review could verify neither the study identity nor that publication listing, and the full paper was not read. No efficacy or follow-up conclusion can be drawn from this material. Global B-cell depletion, regardless of clinical benefit, would require separate evidence of antigen selectivity to demonstrate the proposed innovation.

The psoriasis review describes sustained absence of pathogenic autoantibodies after rituximab treatment in pemphigus as a precedent relevant to disease modification. This is secondary evidence for durable change in an autoantibody-mediated disease, not proof of antigen-selective treatment. Grada's January 5, 2026 perspective further frames lasting remission as a curative challenge involving both immune memory and persistent structural tissue programs, and calls for trials that distinguish modification from suppression.

Evidence boundary: the supplied material supports these dated mechanistic findings and clinical observations but contains no comprehensive update of subsequent developments through November 1, 2026. It therefore does not establish that the complete capability has been achieved, nor does it establish that every relevant approach remains unsuccessful. Missing source text is a limit on interpretation rather than evidence that the reported result is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: after a finite treatment course, show at least two years of drug-free remission in one T-cell-mediated skin disease, such as psoriasis or vitiligo, and one autoantibody-mediated skin disease, such as pemphigus. These are proposed thresholds, not established consensus criteria. Trials should specify disease-appropriate remission definitions, permitted rescue treatment, relapse criteria and stopping rules. A single early CAR-T series or a minority remaining clear for one year after a biologic would not satisfy this proposed demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Two-year drug-free remission in T-cell-mediated and autoantibody-mediated skin diseases

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanistic demonstration: combine longitudinal skin biopsies with functional antigen-specificity assays and sampling of relevant circulating, B-cell and antibody-producing compartments. Show durable loss of pathogenic populations or stable loss of their disease-causing function, and monitor for replacement populations with the same specificity. Prespecify detection limits and sampling coverage. A reprogrammed clone need not disappear, and negative biopsies cannot prove absence throughout the body or exclude all future recurrence.
completion_criteria.label: Durable loss of antigen-specific pathogenic populations or disease-causing function

completion_criteria.text: Proposed protection and tissue demonstration: document retained vaccine or infection responses and assess antiviral and antitumor surveillance separately with appropriate follow-up. For an atopic dermatitis application, require stable barrier function after treatment withdrawal in addition to clinical remission. Persistent tissue injury or structural-cell memory should be measured where relevant rather than assumed to resolve when pathogenic lymphocytes are controlled.
completion_criteria.label: Retained immune responses with assessed surveillance and tissue function

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundary: reproduce durable clinical and mechanistic effects in independent patient cohorts with transparent follow-up, adverse-event reporting and documentation of all ongoing treatment. Establish which antigen specificities, disease stages and patient groups are covered, and whether protection and tissue function persist over the observed interval. Success in finite cohorts would establish demonstrated breadth and durability, not literal universality or lifelong cure.
completion_criteria.label: Independent cohorts reproduce durable effects with documented applicability limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: DER-07, a skin-origin intervention that prevents atopic dermatitis and the atopic march, concerns prevention of disease development and progression. DER-03 concerns established pathogenic immune memory. Either capability might inform the other, but remission after memory editing would not demonstrate prevention of the atopic march.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-08, reconstitution of melanocyte stem cells where the follicular reservoir is gone, addresses replacement of a lost regenerative cell population. DER-03 could help protect restored melanocytes if a pathogenic immune attack remains active, but stopping that attack does not itself rebuild an absent melanocyte stem-cell reservoir.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-01, clinical restoration of a complete human skin organ, has a broader tissue-reconstruction goal. DER-02, a one-time genomic cure of severe monogenic skin disease through epidermal stem cells, corrects an inherited epithelial defect. Both could require attention to immune responses, but neither is defined by antigen-selective editing of established pathogenic immune memory.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-04, programmable passage of macromolecules and gene editors across intact stratum corneum, could provide a delivery route for a future memory-directed intervention. Delivery alone would not establish its immune selectivity or durability. A broadly acting topical cytokine blocker would meet DER-03 only if it additionally demonstrated durable, antigen-selective control after treatment withdrawal.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-05, epidermal DNA repair sufficient to prevent ultraviolet-driven skin cancer, and DER-06, therapeutic reset of the mutant epidermal field, address epithelial damage and mutation. DER-03 targets pathogenic immune memory. Preserving antitumor surveillance is an important boundary for DER-03, but does not substitute for either DNA repair or removal of a mutant epidermal field.

Roster-based synthesis: DER-09, durable regenerative closure of diabetic foot ulcers after ischemia and pressure are treated, and DER-10, reversal of established keloids and pathological cutaneous scars, concern wound repair and tissue remodeling. They overlap with DER-03 in seeking a lasting change rather than continuing suppression, while requiring distinct demonstrations of regenerative closure or scar reversal.

change_log.reason: The review documents both persistent resident memory after treatment and reductions in resident-memory populations with some therapies.

change_log.reason: Structural tissue programs, circulating reservoirs and renewed pathogenic specificities can limit durability and generalization.

change_log.reason: The supplied evidence did not establish the ranking, and the retained Bieber page was a cookie interstitial. Other reviewed sources support the treatment-free-remission goal.

change_log.reason: Preclinical depletion, review-level observations and abstract-only retrospective results support different levels of inference.

change_log.reason: The user requested preservation of unresolved quantitative detail. Missing retained material prevents confirmation but does not establish falsity.

change_log.reason: Biopsies alone cannot prove complete absence, reprogramming need not eliminate clones, and limited vaccine or infection tests cannot establish broad antitumor surveillance.

unresolved_issues: Whether subsequent developments through November 1, 2026 establish any component or complete clinical demonstration remains unresolved because the supplied freshness record contains no comprehensive update.
The TRuE-V counts of 22 of 56 maintaining F-VASI75 and 12 of 56 maintaining F-VASI90 require source confirmation, including endpoint definitions and withdrawal-population details.
The reported 23-patient DSG3 CAAR-T result and the clinical efficacy of antigen-specific CAAR-T cannot be determined from the retained material.
The alleged July 30, 2026 Blood publication on CD19 CAR-T without lymphodepletion, its trial association, results and follow-up remain unverified.
Disease-specific antigen coverage, pathogenic-population coverage and the contributions of circulating reservoirs, antibody-producing compartments and structural-cell memory remain to be established.
The feasibility of preserving broad antiviral and antitumor surveillance while durably controlling pathogenic memory requires direct demonstration.
The two-year, two-disease demonstration is a proposed benchmark; its optimal design, cohort sizes and disease-specific measurements remain to be defined.

The review recommendation to omit unavailable-source numerical assertions was not adopted in full: those details were retained with explicit uncertainty to meet the user's instruction to preserve unresolved quantitative information.

brief.title: Lasting relief by removing harmful skin immune memory
possible: People with recurring skin disease could finish a course of treatment and stay well after it ends. The treatment would remove or permanently disarm the immune cells that remember and restart their particular disease.

It would distinguish harmful cells by the disease-related target they recognize, while preserving useful immune memory. For blistering diseases driven by antibodies—immune proteins that attack the body's own tissue—it would also have to control the cells producing those antibodies.
why: Patients could reduce or end their dependence on continuing medicines that suppress inflammation or immune activity. Treatment would change what keeps the disease returning, giving people lasting relief while retaining protection against infection and cancer.

sources.showed: This perspective describes opportunities and obstacles for treatments that keep inflammatory skin diseases quiet after treatment ends.
sources.cited_for: It explains the goal of lasting disease control without ongoing treatment.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate selective removal of harmful immune memory.

sources.showed: Their review describes mouse experiments that depleted disease-driving memory T cells, immune cells that remember targets, in vitiligo. Other memory T cells were also depleted.
sources.quote: Both lesional and non-lesional skin in vitiligo patients harbor melanocyte-specific CD8+ TRM cells, which predominantly localize to depigmented areas
sources.cited_for: Harmful immune memory can be disrupted, but the mouse treatment also affected other memory cells.
sources.not_established: The experiments do not establish selective, lasting control in people while preserving protective immunity.

sources.showed: This study examines whether vitiligo improvement persists after patients stop ruxolitinib cream.
sources.cited_for: It addresses persistence of clinical improvement after treatment withdrawal.
sources.not_established: Maintained improvement alone would not demonstrate selective removal of harmful immune memory.

sources.showed: Their review describes lasting improvement after psoriasis treatment ends in some patients, alongside persistence of disease-associated memory cells.
sources.quote: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease and some patients experience durable improvement of their skin lesions after therapy, with remission lasting long after discontinuing the medication.
sources.cited_for: Lasting improvement after withdrawal is possible, but its underlying mechanism remains debated.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish that selective removal of harmful memory caused the improvement.

sources.showed: Their retrospective study, which looked back at patient outcomes, found relapse after psoriasis treatment stopped. Selected groups treated early had longer periods without treatment.
sources.cited_for: Treatment timing may matter for lasting disease control in some patients.
sources.not_established: The retrospective design cannot establish that treatment erased harmful immune memory.

sources.showed: This clinical report concerns engineered immune cells designed to target cells making harmful antibodies in pemphigus, an autoimmune blistering disease.
sources.cited_for: It concerns an approach intended to target disease-specific antibody-producing pathways.
sources.not_established: Whether this approach achieves lasting clinical benefit with disease-specific targeting remains unresolved.

sources.showed: This trial listing concerns engineered immune cells targeting B cells, immune cells involved in antibody production.
sources.cited_for: It concerns an approach to controlling the antibody-producing arm of immunity.
sources.not_established: Broad B-cell depletion would require separate proof that it selectively controls disease-causing cells.

sources.showed: This perspective frames lasting remission as a challenge involving both immune memory and persistent changes in skin tissue.
sources.cited_for: Lasting control may require changing the tissue conditions that help disease return.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate that controlling immune memory alone restores healthy tissue or prevents relapse.

shown: The clearest experimental step comes from vitiligo mouse studies described by Su and Liu: treatment depleted harmful memory cells, but also depleted other memory cells. This demonstrates disruption of disease-driving memory with limited selectivity.

In people, some psoriasis patients remain improved after treatment stops. Ranzinger and Eyerich review these observations, and Chen and colleagues report them in a retrospective study. Clinical improvement does not establish that the harmful memory was removed or permanently disarmed.
missing: A treatment must distinguish disease-driving cells from protective cells that share their location or survival signals.
Lasting control must reach harmful cells beyond the skin and prevent replacement cells from restarting disease.
For antibody-driven disease, selective targeting must durably stop harmful antibody production.
Protective immune responses and healthy skin function must persist after treatment ends.

milestones.label: Drug-free remission across distinct disease mechanisms
milestones.explanation: A finite treatment would have to produce two years of drug-free remission in both a T-cell-driven and an antibody-driven skin disease. This would demonstrate lasting benefit across distinct mechanisms.

milestones.label: Lasting loss of harmful cells or their disease-causing activity
milestones.explanation: Repeated skin and relevant body samples would have to show lasting loss or disarming of cells recognizing disease-related targets, without harmful replacements. This would connect remission to control of immune memory.

milestones.label: Protective immunity and healthy skin function persist
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to document retained vaccine or infection responses, assess antiviral and cancer surveillance separately, and test skin barrier stability for atopic dermatitis. This would establish protection and tissue function.

milestones.label: Independent patient groups reproduce lasting effects
milestones.explanation: Independent patient groups would have to reproduce clinical and immune effects, with harms, ongoing treatment and applicability documented. This would establish how broadly and durably the treatment works.

uncertain: Which disease-related targets and cell populations must each treatment cover, and can other cells or persistent tissue changes restart disease?
Can selective control preserve broad protection against viruses and cancer over time?
The proposed remission benchmark still needs disease-specific definitions; meeting it would not establish lifelong protection.

page.title: Antigen-specific immune tolerance in autoimmune skin disease
page.definition: A finite treatment durably controls the harmful immune response to an autoantigen, one of the body's own molecules recognized by the immune system. It may eliminate the cells responsible or suppress their pathogenic activity. Clinical benefit persists after treatment ends, and protective immune responses remain intact.

goal.need: An estimated 29.5 million adults worldwide had physician-diagnosed psoriasis in 2017. Among 400 patients who stopped an interleukin-17 inhibitor after at least 90% improvement in psoriasis severity, median time to relapse was 3.29 months. In pemphigus, broad B-cell depletion can leave patients vulnerable to serious infection. If treatment controls the response to an antigen driving a patient's disease, the patient could remain well without maintenance treatment and retain immune defenses against infection.

figures.caption: Vitiligo response maintained for one year after ruxolitinib cream withdrawal
figures.note: Patients had achieved at least 90% facial improvement before withdrawal. These are observed proportions, not Kaplan–Meier estimates. Clinical persistence does not establish antigen selectivity.

completion.title: A disease-specific clinical response persists after antigen-selective treatment, with protective immunity intact.
completion.criterion: After finite antigen-selective treatment, patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis sustain <1% affected body surface area and Physician Global Assessment 0/1 for >12 months off treatment. In nonsegmental vitiligo, patients with ≥90% improvement from baseline in facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index at withdrawal maintain ≥75% improvement throughout 52 weeks. In pemphigus vulgaris, no new or established lesions are present for ≥2 months off all systemic therapy. In the same patients over the applicable interval, demonstrate sustained control of the pathogenic antigen-specific response, including pathogenic antibodies where relevant, and preservation of protective immune responses.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis. No outside body defines the combined test. Its components come from NIAID, the plaque psoriasis Delphi panel, TRuE-V and the International Pemphigus Committee.
completion.basis: The psoriasis panel proposed its clinical measure in the absence of precise biomarkers. TRuE-V measured time to relapse after withdrawal in patients who had reached 90% facial improvement at week 52. The Atlas uses freedom from relapse throughout the ensuing 52 weeks as its vitiligo criterion. The pemphigus committee defines complete remission off systemic therapy. Each interval establishes durability only for the time observed.

milestones.title: A treatment disables disease-antigen-reactive cells while sparing unrelated cells in vitro.
milestones.criterion: In a functional assay, show that the candidate kills or silences cells recognizing a disease-driving antigen while sparing cells of unrelated specificity tested under the same conditions.
milestones.set_by: Antigen-specific cytotoxicity convention demonstrated in the pemphigus CAAR-T studies of Ellebrecht and colleagues and Lee and colleagues; the published experiments concern pemphigus.
milestones.threshold_quote: specific cytotoxicity against cells expressing anti-Dsg3 BCRs in vitro

milestones.title: An antigen-selective treatment reduces skin-disease pathology in an animal model.
milestones.criterion: In an animal model, show that an antigen-selective candidate reduces both disease manifestations and the implicated autoimmune response relative to a control. In pemphigus, assess blistering clinically and histologically and measure the anti-desmoglein-3 antibody response. In a vitiligo prevention model, assess development of depigmentation and the response to the model antigen.
milestones.set_by: Preclinical therapeutic proof-of-concept convention used in the published pemphigus CAAR-T development programme; no cross-disease numerical efficacy threshold was specified.
milestones.threshold_quote: leading to clinical and histologic resolution of blisters.

milestones.title: An antigen-selective treatment for a skin disease is administered to people in a phase 1 study.
milestones.criterion: Document administration of a candidate directed at a specified disease autoantigen to patients with that disease under a phase I protocol.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1), definition of phase 1 investigation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Clinical responses persist off treatment for >12 months in psoriasis, 52 weeks in vitiligo or ≥2 months in PV.
milestones.criterion: After withdrawal of antigen-selective treatment, apply the measure for the disease studied. In moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, sustain <1% affected body surface area and Physician Global Assessment 0/1 for >12 months. In nonsegmental vitiligo, among patients with ≥90% improvement from baseline in facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index at withdrawal, document no fall below 75% improvement throughout 52 weeks. In pemphigus vulgaris, document absence of new or established lesions, including mucosal lesions, for ≥2 months off all systemic therapy.
milestones.set_by: Atlas application of three clinical measures. The psoriasis Delphi panel and International Pemphigus Committee define their respective criteria. TRuE-V defines relapse during a 52-week withdrawal period. No outside body sets the combined milestone for antigen-selective treatment.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary endpoint was time to relapse (< F-VASI 75)

milestones.title: A clinical study measures the change in antigen-specific lymphocytes after treatment.
milestones.criterion: Measure the frequency of lymphocytes recognizing the target autoantigen in patient samples before and after dosing, alongside changes in the broader lymphocyte populations. The TPM203 study measured circulating desmoglein-3-specific CD4 T cells in pemphigus vulgaris. Its exploratory endpoint specified the measurement without a minimum percentage reduction.
milestones.set_by: TPM203 phase I study, EudraCT 2019-001727-12, published exploratory pharmacodynamic endpoint in pemphigus vulgaris.
milestones.threshold_quote: changes in Dsg3-specific and bulk T- and B-cell frequencies

not_found: No outside body’s integrated pass/fail test combining antigen-selective memory erasure, preserved protective immunity and off-treatment skin remission was located.
No common numerical selectivity or animal-efficacy threshold across these diseases was identified.
Searches did not locate a human demonstration of antigen-selective pathogenic-memory erasure in psoriasis or vitiligo.
The opened ClinicalTrials.gov pages did not expose the REVEAL results or RESET-PV study details.
The full Chen psoriasis cohort paper could not be opened; its quantitative result is supported by the indexed abstract.
No human study in the three diseases was found to demonstrate off-treatment clinical response, sustained antigen-specific control and preserved protective immunity in the same patients.

results.finding: Among 400 patients with plaque psoriasis who stopped IL-17 inhibitors after reaching PASI 90, median time to relapse was 3.29 months.
results.detail: The year of sustained PASI 90 used to define the 141-patient subgroup occurred before withdrawal.
results.quote: Among 400 patients who discontinued treatment after achieving Psoriasis Area and Severity Index 90, the median relapse time was 3.29 months (approximately 14 weeks).

results.finding: DSG3-CAART reduced anti-DSG3 IgG-secreting B cells by 83.1%–92.3% in vitro in the two patient samples with detectable targets.
results.detail: The third patient sample had no detectable anti-DSG3 B cells at baseline. BSA served as a negative antigen control and yielded no detectable responding population to assess for sparing.
results.quote: Coincubation of PV B cells with DSG3-CAART resulted in 83.1%–92.3% reduction in anti-DSG3 IgG B cells, without reduction of total IgG B cells.

results.finding: In 15 mice with active immune pemphigus, DSG3-CAART improved blistering and lowered anti-DSG3 titers until weeks 6–7.
results.detail: Serum anti-DSG3 titers rose again around weeks 6–7 as DSG3-CAART disappeared from peripheral blood. EC5 immunoreactivity persisted.
results.quote: Nevertheless, DSG3-CAART resolved clinical and histologic pathology and reduced serum autoantibodies against pathogenic DSG3 epitopes.

results.finding: Dsg3-Fc killed >90% of engineered Dsg3-reactive B cells in vitro (3 technical replicates per condition).
results.quote: In vitro, Dsg3-Fc selectively eliminated Dsg3-autoreactive B cells.

results.finding: In the active pemphigus model (24 mice), clinical severity was lower with Dsg3-Fc than with IVIG at day 15 (P < 0.0001).

results.finding: Desmoglein 3-directed TPM203 was administered intravenously to 17 patients with pemphigus vulgaris in a phase I trial.
results.detail: Participants had no to moderate disease activity. The trial ended early because of slow recruitment and COVID-19 restrictions.
results.quote:
Thirty-six patients underwent screening and 17 received 
TPM203 (12 in part A, 5 in part B): 13 in Germany, 2 in 
Italy and 2 in the UK.

results.finding: In the single-dose TPM203 cohort with pemphigus vulgaris (n = 12), circulating Dsg3-specific CD4 T-cell frequency fell significantly at week 8.
results.detail: The dextramer assay used ex vivo Dsg3 enrichment. Low cell frequencies limited assessment of individual responses, so the significant result was reported for the pooled single-dose cohort.
results.quote: Dsg3-specific T cells were found to be significantly reduced at week 8 following single administration of TPM203.

definition = "A finite treatment durably controls the harmful immune response to an autoantigen, one of the body's own molecules recognized by the immune system. It may eliminate the cells responsible or suppress their pathogenic activity. Clinical benefit persists after treatment ends, and protective immune responses remain intact.". Reason: The original definition restricts tolerance to elimination or silencing of cells and omits durable regulation of their pathogenic response.

goal.need = "An estimated 29.5 million adults worldwide had physician-diagnosed psoriasis in 2017. Among 400 patients who stopped an interleukin-17 inhibitor after at least 90% improvement in psoriasis severity, median time to relapse was 3.29 months. In pemphigus, broad B-cell depletion can leave patients vulnerable to serious infection. If treatment controls the response to an antigen driving a patient's disease, the patient could remain well without maintenance treatment and retain immune defenses against infection.". Reason: The current text gives a relapse statistic but omits the scale of disease, the benefit of stopping maintenance treatment and the reason antigen selectivity matters to patients.

add statement by Topas Therapeutics GmbH, phase I pemphigus vulgaris protocol TPV11, 2019: "to explore early signs of effectiveness of induction of antigen-specific immune tolerance with TPM203 in pemphigus vulgaris patients". Reason: The registered protocol names a specific skin disease, antigen-directed treatment and clinical objective missing from the two general goal statements.

edit completion: title = "A disease-specific clinical response persists after antigen-selective treatment, with protective immunity intact."; criterion = "After finite antigen-selective treatment, patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis sustain <1% affected body surface area and Physician Global Assessment 0/1 for >12 months off treatment. In nonsegmental vitiligo, patients with \u226590% improvement from baseline in facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index at withdrawal maintain \u226575% improvement throughout 52 weeks. In pemphigus vulgaris, no new or established lesions are present for \u22652 months off all systemic therapy. In the same patients over the applicable interval, demonstrate sustained control of the pathogenic antigen-specific response, including pathogenic antibodies where relevant, and preservation of protective immune responses."; set_by = "Atlas synthesis. No outside body defines the combined test. Its components come from NIAID, the plaque psoriasis Delphi panel, TRuE-V and the International Pemphigus Committee."; basis = "The psoriasis panel proposed its clinical measure in the absence of precise biomarkers. TRuE-V measured time to relapse after withdrawal in patients who had reached 90% facial improvement at week 52. The Atlas uses freedom from relapse throughout the ensuing 52 weeks as its vitiligo criterion. The pemphigus committee defines complete remission off systemic therapy. Each interval establishes durability only for the time observed."; refs = [3, 5, 2, 6]. Reason: The current test extends the psoriasis and vitiligo measures beyond their source populations and calls facial repigmentation and mucosal pemphigus remission skin remission.

edit m1: criterion = "In a functional assay, show that the candidate kills or silences cells recognizing a disease-driving antigen while sparing cells of unrelated specificity tested under the same conditions."; refs = [4, 7, 16]. Reason: The criterion contains results from a three-patient experiment and omits the earlier controlled demonstration of antigen selectivity in cultured cells.

edit m2: criterion = "In an animal model, show that an antigen-selective candidate reduces both disease manifestations and the implicated autoimmune response relative to a control. In pemphigus, assess blistering clinically and histologically and measure the anti-desmoglein-3 antibody response. In a vitiligo prevention model, assess development of depigmentation and the response to the model antigen."; refs = [4, 7, 12]. Reason: Mouse counts and antibody rebound describe an individual experiment, while the milestone tests improvement in both disease manifestations and the implicated immune response.

edit m3: criterion = "Document administration of a candidate directed at a specified disease autoantigen to patients with that disease under a phase I protocol."; refs = [8, 9, 13, 15]. Reason: The criterion mixes phase I administration with efficacy results and a CD19-directed comparator, while omitting the published antigen-directed TPM203 trial.

add milestone after m3: "A clinical study measures the change in antigen-specific lymphocytes after treatment.". Reason: The existing sequence jumps from dosing to clinical durability and misses the human measurement of antigen-specific lymphocytes used in the pemphigus trial.

edit m4: title = "Clinical responses persist off treatment for >12 months in psoriasis, 52 weeks in vitiligo or \u22652 months in PV."; criterion = "After withdrawal of antigen-selective treatment, apply the measure for the disease studied. In moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, sustain <1% affected body surface area and Physician Global Assessment 0/1 for >12 months. In nonsegmental vitiligo, among patients with \u226590% improvement from baseline in facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index at withdrawal, document no fall below 75% improvement throughout 52 weeks. In pemphigus vulgaris, document absence of new or established lesions, including mucosal lesions, for \u22652 months off all systemic therapy."; set_by = "Atlas application of three clinical measures. The psoriasis Delphi panel and International Pemphigus Committee define their respective criteria. TRuE-V defines relapse during a 52-week withdrawal period. No outside body sets the combined milestone for antigen-selective treatment."; set_by_kind = "atlas"; threshold_quote = "The primary endpoint was time to relapse (< F-VASI 75)"; threshold_ref = 2; refs = [5, 2, 6]. Reason: The vitiligo protocol defines relapse and a follow-up period, while the requirement to remain relapse-free throughout that period is the Atlas's application of the protocol.
